title: WPSB/204/2014 of Dr. Radha Sharma Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No. 204 of 2014 (S/B)
Dr. Radha Sharma. ..... Petitioner.
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others. ..... Respondents.
Mr. Arvind K. Sharma, Advocate for the applicant/petitioner.
Mr. Subhash Uppadhyay, Chief Standing Counsel with Mr. Ravindra Singh Bisht, Brief Holder for the
State/respondent nos. 1 & 2.
Mr. B.D. Kandpal, Advocate for Uttarakhand Public Service Commission/respondent no.3.
Dated: September 19, 2014
Coram :Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.
 Hon'ble Alok Singh, J.
Hon'ble Alok Singh, J. (Oral):
CLMA No. 10575/14 (Impleadment Application) &
CLMA No. 10734/14 (Delay Condonation Application) &
MCC No. 754/14 (Recall Application)
IN
Writ Petition No. 204 of 2014 (S/B)
 Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused
the record.
 Mr. Arvind Kumar Sharma, Advocate for the
applicant/petitioner does not wish to press these
applications, since the same have been moved on behalf of
one Mr. Dheeraj Rawat, who was not party in the writ
petition.
 Consequently, all these three applications are
hereby dismissed as not pressed.
CLMA No. 10568/14 (Delay Condonation Application)
In
MCC No. 743/14 (Recall application)
 This is an application seeking condonation of 38
days' delay in moving the recall/review application.
 Learned counsel appearing for the respondents have
no serious objection, if delay is condoned. Therefore, the

2
delay condonation application is allowed. Delay of 38
days' in moving the review/recall application is hereby
condoned.
MCC No. 743/14 (Recall application)
 It is stated by Mr. Arvind Kumar Sharma, Advocate
for the petitioner/applicant that in Writ Petition No.
248/2014 (S/B), this Court was pleased to direct the
Commission to publish the waiting list, prepared in the
year 2012. According to Mr. Sharma, same order ought to
have been passed in the present petition.
 Mr. B.D. Kandpal, Advocate appearing for the
Commission as well as Mr. Subhash Uppadhyay, Chief
Standing Counsel appearing for the State vehemently
argued that life of waiting list is only for one year,
therefore, the same shall not create any right in favour of
the candidates, shown in the waiting list.
 Be that, as it may. It is important to mention here
that in the present petition, the petitioner is not seeking
any mandamus to grant him appointment as per waiting
list. Since, in the Writ Petition No. 248 of 2014 (S/B), this
Court was pleased to direct the Commission to publish the
waiting list and to send the same to the State
Government, in order to maintain judicial discipline, we
recall/review the order under review i.e. order dated
08.07.2014 and dispose of instant writ petition in terms of
order dated 25.07.2014 passed in Writ Petition No. 248 of
2014 S/B.
(Alok Singh, J.) (V.K.Bist, J.)
 19.09.2014
